text:
Re: Dominic Sato, 34

Dominic landed awkwardly from a jump playing basketball 3 days ago and felt something tear just below his left kneecap. He cannot straight-leg raise and walks with the knee locked straight in a splint. The patella sits visibly higher than on the right, with a palpable gap below it. X-ray: patella alta, small bony fleck at the inferior pole. He is a personal trainer.

Dr Emily Quach
note: Acute patellar tendon rupture with loss of extensor mechanism; early surgical repair is time-critical.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Andrea Kalinowski, 47

Andrea felt pain in her left calf lunging for a ball at tennis 8 days ago. ED diagnosed a calf strain and advised rest. She is still limping and cannot stand on her toes. Today I found a palpable gap in the tendon about 5 cm above the heel and the calf squeeze test is absent on that side. Ultrasound this afternoon: complete Achilles tendon tear with a 3 cm gap in neutral.

Dr Ben Halloran
note: Acute complete Achilles rupture initially missed as a calf strain, now 8 days old; the management decision is time-critical. Hard because the ED diagnosis of calf strain could anchor the reader.

text:
Re: Wayne Tipoki, 51

Wayne is a removalist. Four days ago he was carrying a fridge down stairs when he felt something give way in the crook of his right elbow, with a sharp pain. There is now a large bruise on the inner forearm and the muscle at the front of his arm looks bunched up near the shoulder. Turning his hand palm-up is weak. No imaging yet. Smoker, 15 a day.

Dr Lucy Barnard
note: Clinical acute distal biceps rupture in a manual worker; early repair is time-critical. Hard because it is described only in lay terms.

text:
Re: Craig Mullins, 45, electrician

Craig fell from a ladder 3 weeks ago and dislocated his left shoulder, which was reduced in ED. He has been in a sling. Pain has improved but he still cannot raise the arm away from his side or reach behind his back, and lift-off and belly-press tests are weak. Deltoid sensation and contraction are normal. Ultrasound: full-thickness tears of supraspinatus and subscapularis with retraction.

Dr Nadia Hussein
note: Acute traumatic cuff tear after dislocation in a working-age patient; early repair is time-critical.

text:
Re: Chloe Antonelli, 17

Chloe twisted her right knee landing at netball 10 days ago. She cannot fully straighten it; it stops about 20 degrees short and she walks on tiptoe. There is a moderate effusion and lateral joint line tenderness. MRI: displaced bucket-handle tear of the lateral meniscus in the notch with a bone bruise; ACL intact. She is in Year 11 and on crutches.

Dr Patrick Ngata
note: Locked knee from a displaced bucket-handle tear in an adolescent; early repair to preserve the meniscus.

text:
Re: Sean Gallagher, 40

Sean caught his right foot under a bin trolley 2 weeks ago and twisted it. He was told it was a sprain. He is still unable to push off and has midfoot swelling with bruising on the sole of the foot. Weight-bearing X-ray today: 3 mm diastasis between the bases of the first and second metatarsals, with a small fleck of bone in the gap. He is a warehouse worker.

Dr Kate Lindberg
note: Unstable Lisfranc injury two weeks old; fixation is time-critical. Hard because it is framed as a sprain and the diastasis is described without naming the injury.

text:
Dear Dr,

Re: Owen Matagi, 23

Owen fell off his skateboard onto his left hand 2 weeks ago. Initial X-rays were reported normal but he remained tender over the scaphoid, so I arranged a CT: fracture through the proximal pole of the scaphoid, displaced by about 1.5 mm. He has been in a thumb spica splint since my first review. He is a chef and left-handed.

Kind regards,
Dr Hayley Burke
note: Displaced proximal pole scaphoid fracture with high non-union risk; surgical fixation decision is time-critical.

text:
Re: Margaret Sloane, 55

Margaret fell onto her right shoulder walking the dog 10 days ago. She was seen at an after-hours clinic and given a sling. She came in today because she still cannot lift the arm. X-ray: fracture of the greater tuberosity of the humerus, displaced superiorly by about 8 mm; the humeral head is in joint. Neurovascularly intact. She works as a school administrator.

Dr Julian Faraday
note: Displaced greater tuberosity fracture (>5 mm) in a working-age patient, referred late; fixation should not be delayed.

text:
Re: Erin Haddad, 36

Erin hurt her left thumb in a fall while skiing at Thredbo 6 days ago, with the pole still in her hand. She calls it a sprained thumb. There is bruising and swelling over the ulnar side of the thumb MCP joint with a small firm lump there. Stressing the joint at 30 degrees of flexion opens it widely with no firm endpoint. X-ray: no fracture. Ultrasound suggests a Stener lesion.

Dr Michael Odell
note: Complete thumb UCL rupture with a Stener lesion needs early surgical repair. Hard because the patient calls it a sprain and the X-ray is normal.

text:
Dear Neurologist,

Re: Henrik Johansen, 58

Over the last 6 weeks Henrik has developed weakness and numbness in both legs and now both hands. He needs the rail to climb stairs and has dropped cups. On examination: symmetrical proximal and distal weakness, 4-/5 in the legs, reflexes absent throughout, glove-and-stocking sensory loss. No breathing or swallowing problems; FVC on the practice spirometer 3.6 L. B12, glucose and TSH normal.

Dr Grace Ahn
note: Subacute progressive symmetrical weakness with areflexia suggesting CIDP or a GBS variant; nerve conduction studies and an early immunotherapy decision are time-critical. No respiratory or bulbar features, which would mean ED.

text:
Re: Beryl Hatfield, 76

Beryl has a heart murmur known for years. Over the last 2 months she has become breathless walking to her letterbox and has had two episodes of feeling faint while walking uphill. Echo last week: severe calcific aortic stenosis, aortic valve area 0.7 cm2, mean gradient 48 mmHg, LVEF 55%. She lives independently and still drives.

Meds: perindopril 4 mg, atorvastatin.

Dr Robert Kingsley
note: Severe symptomatic aortic stenosis with exertional presyncope; an early valve-intervention decision (TAVI/AVR) is time-critical.

text:
Re: Desmond Clarke, 79

Desmond's wife noticed a lump on his scalp about 6 weeks ago that he thought was a pimple. It has grown quickly and is now a firm, dome-shaped pink nodule of 12 mm that bleeds when he combs his hair. No pigment visible on dermoscopy, just irregular vessels. He had several BCCs removed in the past. No palpable cervical nodes.

Dr Samantha Ivey
note: Rapidly growing bleeding nodule raises concern for amelanotic nodular melanoma or aggressive SCC; urgent excision. Hard because it is described as a pimple and lacks pigment.

text:
Re: Clive Barrington, 71

Clive has had intermittent right shoulder ache for about 2 years, worse after gardening. No injury. He can lift his arm fully overhead and his strength is reasonable, with mild weakness of external rotation. Ultrasound: small 1 cm full-thickness supraspinatus tear with tendinosis and acromioclavicular arthritis. Paracetamol and a home exercise program keep him comfortable most of the time. He would like advice on long-term management.

Dr Anita Rao
note: Small degenerative full-thickness cuff tear in an older patient with good function; non-operative care is first line. Hard because 'full-thickness tear' could trigger urgent.

text:
Re: Rosemary Klein, 63

Rosemary has had pain at the back of her left heel for over a year. It limits walking to about 20 minutes and she has stopped her bushwalking group. Shoe backs rub on a bony bump. She has done heel lifts, a loading program and shockwave therapy. There is a thickened tender insertion and a Haglund prominence on X-ray. Ultrasound: insertional tendinopathy with retrocalcaneal bursitis, no tear.

Dr Felix Ambrose
note: Chronic insertional Achilles tendinopathy with Haglund deformity, failing conservative care with limited walking; disability without deterioration risk.

text:
Re: Leonard Fisk, 66

Leonard ruptured his right distal biceps tendon about 18 months ago. He chose not to have surgery at the time. He has full elbow movement, plays bowls and does his own home maintenance. He notices that his forearm tires turning a screwdriver and he gets occasional cramping in the arm. No pain at rest. He has asked whether surgery is still an option.

Dr Clara Whitfield
note: Old untreated distal biceps rupture that is functioning well; the time-critical window has passed. Hard because 'distal biceps rupture' is a classic urgent phrase.

text:
Re: Jessica Moran, 30

Jessica had an open reduction and internal fixation of a right ankle fracture 9 months ago. The fracture has united on X-ray and she is back to running. The lateral plate is prominent and rubs on her ski boots and work shoes, and she has asked about having the metalwork removed. No signs of infection.

Dr Hamish Doyle
note: Healed ankle fracture with symptomatic hardware; elective removal.

text:
Re: Vikram Nair, 36

Vikram has 4 months of lateral right knee pain that began while squatting at the gym. He describes an occasional click but the knee has never locked or given way, and he has full range. Mild lateral joint line tenderness, no effusion. MRI: small radial tear of the body of the lateral meniscus, ACL intact, cartilage normal. He is modifying his training and working full time.

Dr Elise Moffat
note: Stable meniscal tear with no locking or true mechanical block; non-urgent.

text:
Re: Donna Leclair, 52

Donna is a hairdresser with 14 months of lateral left elbow pain. She has had physiotherapy, a brace, a steroid injection and a PRP injection. It hurts to hold scissors and hairdryers, and she has cut her hours to 3 days a week. Ultrasound: common extensor origin tendinosis with a small partial-thickness tear. Full elbow range, no neurological signs.

Dr Tim Boulos
note: Chronic lateral epicondylalgia with a partial tear, failing conservative care and reducing work; pain and disability without risk of rapid deterioration.

text:
Re: Aaron Pritchard, 38

Aaron is a keen runner with 5 months of pain under his left heel on getting out of bed and at the start of runs. He has reduced his mileage. Tender at the plantar fascia origin, normal neurological examination. He has started calf stretching and bought new running shoes, with some improvement. Ultrasound: plantar fascia thickened to 6 mm. He is wondering whether an injection would help.

Dr Megan Loh
note: Plantar fasciitis, improving with early conservative care.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Renee Castellano, 45

Renee describes her left shoulder pain as excruciating and says she has not had a full night's sleep in months. It came on without injury 7 months ago. External rotation is reduced to about 20 degrees, with restricted abduction. X-ray normal. She has type 1 diabetes. A hydrodilatation 3 months ago helped for a few weeks. She is struggling to dress and to do her hair.

Dr Philip Moss
note: Adhesive capsulitis with significant pain and disability but no time-critical decision. Hard because the dramatic language suggests acute urgency.

text:
Re: Melanie Kruger, 68

Melanie fell onto her outstretched right arm 3 weeks ago. X-ray showed an undisplaced radial head fracture. She has been in a collar-and-cuff and has started gentle movement. She now has full forearm rotation and is about 15 degrees short of full elbow extension, improving each week. Pain is mild. Repeat X-ray: no displacement.

Dr Christopher Lam
note: Undisplaced radial head fracture with no mechanical block, recovering well.

text:
Re: Holly Brennan, 35

Holly is a masters swimmer with 5 months of gradually worsening pain at the front of her right shoulder during freestyle training. No injury. She has full range and full strength, with positive impingement signs. Ultrasound: partial-thickness articular-side tear of supraspinatus, about 30% thickness, with tendinosis. She has reduced her training and has begun a rotator cuff program with a physio.

Dr Gabriel Stone
note: Atraumatic partial-thickness cuff tear with full strength in a young swimmer; non-operative care is standard.

text:
Re: Martin Okafor, 44

Martin felt a sudden sharp pain in the middle of his right calf while playing tennis a week ago, as if he had been hit by a ball. He is now walking with a limp and there is bruising down to the ankle. The Achilles tendon is intact on palpation and the calf squeeze test is normal. Ultrasound: partial tear of the medial head of gastrocnemius with a small haematoma; Achilles intact.

Dr Jade Whitmore
note: 'Tennis leg' (medial gastrocnemius tear) with an intact Achilles; managed conservatively. Hard because the story closely mimics an Achilles rupture.

text:
Re: Roberto Salinas, 50

Roberto ruptured his left Achilles tendon 14 weeks ago and chose non-operative management in a functional boot under the fracture clinic, which has now discharged him. He is out of the boot, walking without a limp and can do 8 single-leg heel raises. His physiotherapist has asked for specialist advice on when he can safely return to jogging and social soccer.

Dr Naomi Pearce
note: Healing, functionally treated Achilles rupture with a return-to-sport question.

text:
Re: Imogen Hart, 32

Imogen had a CXR for a persistent cough after a cold, which showed bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, confirmed on CT, with no lung parenchymal changes. The cough has since settled. She has tender red lumps on both shins and has had ankle pain for 3 weeks. Calcium normal, ACE elevated. No weight loss, night sweats or breathlessness. She is otherwise well.

Dr Warren Ellis
note: Probable Lofgren-type sarcoidosis, typically self-limiting; needs specialist confirmation but not urgent.

text:
Re: Colin Fraser, 57

Colin has had heartburn for over 15 years, controlled on esomeprazole 20 mg daily. If he stops it the symptoms come back within days. No dysphagia, vomiting, bleeding, weight loss or anaemia. He has never had a gastroscopy. He is overweight (BMI 31), ex-smoker, and his brother has Barrett's oesophagus. He would like screening for Barrett's.

Dr Lena Fogarty
note: Long-standing controlled reflux with Barrett's risk factors and no alarm features.

text:
Dear Doctor,

Re: Raymond Chen, 58

Raymond has had 3 weeks of central chest tightness when walking up hills or hurrying for the train, relieved within a few minutes of rest. No symptoms at rest. Smoker of 30 pack-years, hypertension and hyperlipidaemia. ECG at rest normal. Troponin normal. I have started aspirin, a statin and a GTN spray, and advised him to call an ambulance for any pain at rest.

Dr Kirsten Holt
note: New-onset stable exertional angina in a high-risk patient; needs urgent assessment.

text:
Re: Dorothy Ames, 72

Dorothy has had a tremor in both hands for about 10 years, slowly worse, which runs in her family. It is worse when holding a cup or writing and improves with a glass of wine. No rest tremor, rigidity or slowness, and her gait is normal. Propranolol helped but made her dizzy. She would like to discuss other treatments.

Dr Sunil Mathews
note: Slowly progressive essential tremor; minimal dysfunction.

text:
Re: Priyanka Desai, 26

Priyanka has had atopic dermatitis since childhood that has become much worse over the past year, now affecting her face, neck, flexures and hands, roughly 30% of her body surface. She has used potent topical steroids and two courses of oral prednisolone, and stopped ciclosporin because of high blood pressure. The itch wakes her most nights and she has missed work.

Dr Lauren Bishop
note: Severe atopic dermatitis failing systemic therapy, suitable for biologic assessment; major quality-of-life impact but not at risk of rapid deterioration.

text:
Re: Elliot Vance, 61

Elliot had a CT coronary angiogram that incidentally showed a 6 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe. A repeat CT at 6 months shows no change in size. He is an ex-smoker (20 pack-years, quit 15 years ago), with no cough, haemoptysis or weight loss. The radiologist has suggested further surveillance. I would appreciate your advice on ongoing follow-up.

Dr Hollie Garrett
note: Stable small pulmonary nodule under surveillance.
